newsitem.title: USA: Home State to cease writing new business.
newsitem.headline: Home State to cease writing new business.

text.p: Home State Holdings Inc. said Thursday its subsidiaries will cease writing new business after discussions between the property casualty insurer and potential investors ended.
The company, which operates primarily in New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Delaware, said it is still exploring the possible sale of its subsidiaries to third parties.
Any subsidiaries that are not sold will wind up their affairs, said the company, whose strategy was to operate in states that the insurance industry viewed as relatively unattractive.
Home State also said it is in violation of certain covenants in agreements with its banks and its subordinated note holders.
The company said it is unlikely that the proceeds from a sale of its subsidiary and other assets will be enough to pay off those obligations.
Home State also said it has ended its relationship with its banker, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.

The New York state insurance department has asked Home Mutual Insurance Co., a managed mutual based in Binghamton, N.Y., and New York Merchant Bakers Insurance Co. to cease accepting renewals of existing policies, with the exception of personal auto business at New York Merchant Bakers, Home State said.
The subsidiaries that will cease writing new business include Home State Insurance Co., Quaker City Insurance Co., Pinnacle Insurance Co., Westbrook Insurance Co. and New York Merchant Bakers.
Subsidiaries based in Connecticut, Georgia, New Jersey and Pennsylvania are under administrative supervision in those states, the companies said.
In addition, regulators in some of those states may appoint a receiver to manage the operations of the subsidiaries, Home State said.
